text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Attempted assassination of Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov a year ago remains an unsolved mystery. Macedonia preserved its stability despite attempts by assassins to destabilise the country .

- Duty free regime enters into force between Yugoslavia and Macedonia on October 7. Trade between the two countries expected to reach $1 billion. Macedonia wants the border crossing Blace-General Jankovic to be opened for cargo traffic.
- Macedonian and Serbian academies of arts and sciences sign cooperation agreement in Belgrade on Wednesday.

- Macedonia can qualify for first installment of $40 million World Bank SAL credit after it completes privatisation of 880 companies, 40 loss makers and 20 agricultural enterprises. For the second installment, privatisation of 70 percent of the agricultural sector demanded.
- Macedonian airlines Palair Macedonia was grounded over 6.5 million German mark outstanding debt for airport services to Macedonia's public airport company.
